segment_name: Electronic Warfare / Spectrum Awareness adjacent to C4ISR
what_it_does: This layer senses, characterizes, geolocates and visualizes the electromagnetic environment (friendly, neutral, adversary emitters and interference), plans and deconflicts friendly spectrum use (frequency assignment, Joint Restricted Frequency List, EMI resolution), and connects electronic-support (ES) sensing to command and control so commanders can see their own electromagnetic signature, detect and locate adversary emitters, and task electronic-attack or maneuver responses. In C4ISR terms it is the RF-domain COLLECT/PROCESS/FUSE feed into the common operating picture (COP), plus the spectrum-management workflow (DoD Spectrum XXI / GEMSIS / EMBM-J at the enterprise level, EWPMT and Raven Claw and now EWPMT-X on TAK at Army tactical echelons, USMC Spectrum Services Framework, Navy Real Time Spectrum Operations). Kinetic or effects layers (jammers, HPM such as Epirus Leonidas) are adjacent but not C4ISR.

sub_taxonomy.name: Tactical spectrum situational awareness (own-signature and threat emitter sensing)
sub_taxonomy.note: Low-cost networked RF sensors (Army S2AS, Heaviside MOTH, RII Dragonfly, Distributed Spectrum, CACI/Mastodon manpacks, Anduril Pulsar as sensor-effector) feeding a unit-level EM COP. This is where 2025-2026 Army money is moving (REWSI production IDIQs Aug-Sep 2026).

sub_taxonomy.name: Electromagnetic battle management / EW planning (EMBM)
sub_taxonomy.note: Planning, course-of-action analysis, effects visualization and EW tasking: Army EWPMT (Raytheon) and Raven Claw, now pivoting to EWPMT-X on the TAK framework with USMC; DISA Electromagnetic Battle Management-Joint (EMBM-J) for the joint level.

sub_taxonomy.name: Spectrum management and frequency assignment (enterprise and tactical)
sub_taxonomy.note: DISA Defense Spectrum Organization GEMSIS program of record (Spectrum XXI, Joint Spectrum Data Repository, E2ESS, Integrated Spectrum Desktop), NTIA frequency assignment workflow, JRFL building, EMI resolution; USMC Spectrum Services Framework; Navy RTSO/AESOP. Legacy, enterprise-hosted, connectivity-dependent.

sub_taxonomy.name: Passive RF sensing for airspace / C-UAS and installation protection
sub_taxonomy.note: Hidden Level ($100M OTA Aug 2026), Dedrone/Axon, SkySafe, BlueHalo (AeroVironment). Overlaps C-UAS segment; buyer is often JIATF-401, NORTHCOM installations, ranges, border.

sub_taxonomy.name: Interference detection and geolocation (dual-use)
sub_taxonomy.note: Commercial and government spectrum monitoring networks (CRFS RFeye, Rohde & Schwarz, Keysight, KrakenSDR TDOA/AoA), spectrum-sharing enforcement in bands DoD shares with commercial users (context: GAO-26-107873 on DoD-NTIA sharing studies).

sub_taxonomy.name: EW mission data / reprogramming and emitter libraries
sub_taxonomy.note: Air Force 350th Spectrum Warfare Wing, service reprogramming centers; classified threat libraries pushed to sensors and jammers. Mostly classified; least startup-accessible.

sub_taxonomy.name: Effects (electronic attack, HPM, directed energy)
sub_taxonomy.note: Adjacent, not C4ISR: Epirus Leonidas IFPC-HPM, Anduril Pulsar jamming modes, Raytheon NGJ, Lockheed/Northrop SEWIP, BAE aircraft EW. Included for incumbent mapping only.

current_architecture.description: A two-tier architecture. Enterprise tier: DISA DSO's GEMSIS family (Spectrum XXI for frequency assignment requests to NTIA and engineering analysis; Joint Spectrum Data Repository; E2ESS; Integrated Spectrum Desktop) plus the cloud-hosted, service-oriented Electromagnetic Battle Management-Joint (EMBM-J) being built on the GEMSIS foundation. Tactical tier: service-specific tools, chiefly Army EWPMT (Raytheon) with the Raven Claw laptop variant that works without a host server, now being re-hosted as EWPMT-X on the TAK framework with the USMC, and USMC Spectrum Services Framework and Navy RTSO said to interoperate through a common data layer. Sensors (TLS-BCT Manpack, TLS-EAB, MFEW-AL pod on Gray Eagle from 2026, MOTH, Dragonfly on Intrepid 1200 UAS, CACI manpacks, Pulsar) feed detections into ATAK/TAK and the CEMA cell; S2AS adds own-signature sensing and visualization for command posts. Integration between sensor detections, TAK COP, EWPMT planning and the enterprise frequency database is partial and largely manual (INFERENCE from the EWPMT cancellation rationale and the EMBM RFI).

current_architecture.security_domain: Mixed. Own-signature sensing, commercial-band interference hunting and open spectrum monitoring are unclassified/CUI. Threat emitter libraries, EW mission data, SIGINT-derived detections, JSDR frequency assignments and operational spectrum plans are CUI to SECRET and above; joint EMBM runs on classified networks. Coalition sharing constrained by releasability.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: Enterprise spectrum tools (Spectrum XXI, EMBM-J cloud) require reach-back; Raven Claw was created specifically because EWPMT needed a host server and reliable connectivity. Sensor networks depend on tactical radios or mesh for TDOA/AoA fusion; DDIL degrades geolocation accuracy and timeliness.
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Frequency assignment and JRFL updates stall (manual paper/spreadsheet workaround); distributed geolocation loses time-synchronized cross-sensor data; EM COP goes stale; EW tasking reverts to voice and chat; own-signature reporting to higher echelons is delayed.

technical_difficulty.summary: Building a single spectrum sensor or a dashboard is easy; building a calibrated, time-synchronized, low-SWaP sensor network that geolocates emitters accurately in cluttered terrain under DDIL, classifies unknown or LPI/LPD waveforms, and fuses into TAK/EWPMT/JSDR with proper security handling is hard. RF hardware expertise (receiver front-ends, calibration, antennas), signal processing (TDOA/AoA/FDOA, detection in dense environments), distributed systems (edge-cloud sync, mesh), and security architecture (CUI/classified data segregation) are all required. Own-signature awareness (S2AS-type) is the most software-tractable sub-problem; adversary emitter identification against classified libraries is the least.
required_expertise: RF systems and SDR (receiver chains, calibration, antenna arrays)
DSP and emitter geolocation (TDOA, AoA, FDOA, multilateration, propagation modeling over terrain)
RF machine learning (modulation recognition, anomaly detection, open-set classification)
Distributed edge computing and time synchronization (GPS-denied timing)
Tactical networking and DDIL-tolerant data sync
Geospatial visualization and propagation modeling (ITM/Longley-Rice, SPLAT-like tools)
Security architecture for CUI/classified data and cross-domain flows
Ruggedization and EMC of small sensors
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Accurate, trustworthy geolocation and identification of adversary emitters from cheap, imperfectly synchronized sensors in real terrain, delivered to the COP within seconds under contested networks, without leaking friendly information - and doing it against waveforms whose signatures are classified.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: SDRs (USRP, Sidekiq, AIR-T, KrakenSDR), GPS-disciplined clocks, Jetson-class edge GPUs, GNU Radio/SigMF tooling, open-source propagation models, TAK server and plugin SDK, cloud GIS stacks.

capital_intensity.assumptions: PoC assumes 4-10 COTS SDR nodes, a TAK plugin and a cloud/edge fusion service built by two founders plus contractors. Credible demo assumes ruggedized enclosures, participation in an Army TiC exercise or JIATF-401/C-UAS test event, SBIR Phase I/II or an AFWERX open topic, one cleared advisor and initial ITAR compliance program. First production assumes tens to hundreds of sensors, environmental qualification, ATO/RMF, sustainment, and 12-24 months of working capital before IDIQ task orders fund deliveries. Hardware-heavy plays (Hidden Level, Distributed Spectrum) needed $25M-plus equity before a $100M-class ceiling award; a pure software/TAK plugin play could stay under $3M through first fielding.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - own-signature sensing, ISM/commercial-band interference, range and installation monitoring, and public SigMF datasets are unclassified; adversary emitter identification, threat libraries and operational spectrum plans are not.
regulatory_access.government_data_required: For an EM COP or spectrum-management tool: JSDR/Spectrum XXI frequency assignments (CUI), JRFL, unit task organization and emitter parametrics (CUI to SECRET). For own-signature and interference tools: mostly government-owned emissions recorded at exercises under CUI handling.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: ITAR USML Category XI covers military electronics including EW, SIGINT and direction-finding systems and software specially designed for them, plus related technical data; commercial spectrum-monitoring software on COTS SDRs may fall under EAR (e.g., 5A001/5D001 or EAR99) depending on design intent and specifications. Classification is jurisdiction-specific and needs a commodity jurisdiction/classification review by export counsel - no definitive judgment here.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: yes - nearly all DoD-specific data (frequency plans, unit signatures, sensor positions) will be CUI from the first exercise onward.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: yes for adversary emitter ID, EW mission data, joint EMBM and most SIGINT-adjacent use; possibly avoidable for own-signature, interference geolocation and C-UAS passive sensing.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: Not strictly required for an unclassified TAK plugin or interference tool; required within 12-24 months to integrate with EWPMT-X/EMBM-J or classified emitter data.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: If the product is ITAR-controlled (likely for anything marketed as EW/ES/DF for military use), disclosure of technical data to a non-U.S.-person co-founder is a deemed export requiring DDTC authorization or a compartmented structure; the German founder's status as a future permanent resident changes his position (U.S. person under ITAR once lawfully admitted for permanent residence) but not the Indonesian founder's. Foreign ownership/control by non-U.S. persons can also trigger FOCI mitigation for any facility clearance and affect SBIR eligibility (majority U.S.-owned requirement). Scoping the initial product to EAR-controlled or EAR99 dual-use spectrum monitoring is the usual mitigation, but all of this requires specialist export-control and immigration counsel.

unsolved_pain.pain: Commanders cannot see their own command-post electromagnetic signature in real time and cannot report it to higher echelons, a lethal gap given Ukraine-style signature-based targeting.
unsolved_pain.evidence: Army stood up S2AS as an FY25 new start with COTS/NDI sources sought and prioritized transforming-in-contact divisions for demos, with a rapid fielding decision targeted for Q2 FY26.
unsolved_pain.label: FACT

unsolved_pain.pain: The Army's flagship EW planning and management tool never converged on requirements after a decade; the follow-on competition was cancelled and the capability is being re-hosted on TAK.
unsolved_pain.evidence: Army press release on EWPMT task order cancellation citing evolving requirements and strategic realignment; EWPMT-X pilot on TAK with USMC to replace EWPMT in FY2026.
unsolved_pain.label: FACT

unsolved_pain.pain: Units lacked cheap, numerous spectrum sensors; the Army had to create a rapid call-for-solutions path outside its programs of record to buy them.
unsolved_pain.evidence: REWSI call for solutions announced April 2026 followed within five months by ~$196M in production IDIQs to two non-traditional vendors.
unsolved_pain.label: FACT

unsolved_pain.pain: Joint EMSO governance and oversight are fragmented; DoD lacked clear roles and a way to assess EMS superiority.
unsolved_pain.evidence: GAO-21-64 (Dec 2020) on EMSO governance; AOC's Feb 2026 proposal for a JEMSO Combat Support Agency argues for unified enterprise management and senior advocacy still missing.
unsolved_pain.label: FACT

unsolved_pain.pain: Enterprise spectrum management runs on legacy, server-dependent tools (Spectrum XXI, JSDR) that require sustainment and are being slowly wrapped by a cloud EMBM rather than replaced.
unsolved_pain.evidence: DISA sources sought for GEMSIS Sustainment and Enhancement (Sept 2024); EMBM-J being built on the GEMSIS foundation; GAO-22-105221 on agencies' spectrum IT.
unsolved_pain.label: FACT

unsolved_pain.pain: Tactical EW planning tools depended on host servers and connectivity; the Army had to spin off a laptop version (Raven Claw) to work disconnected.
unsolved_pain.evidence: Raven Claw described as a mobile EWPMT variant intended to work without a host server or reliable connection to external data.
unsolved_pain.label: FACT

unsolved_pain.pain: Integrated SIGINT/EW sensor programs (TLS-BCT, MFEW-AL) slipped for years, leaving units with ad hoc kits.
unsolved_pain.evidence: TLS-BCT funding altered repeatedly to speed the manpack; MFEW-AL described as much delayed with 2026 entry as a Gray Eagle pod.
unsolved_pain.label: FACT

unsolved_pain.pain: Service spectrum tools (Army EWPMT, USMC SSF, Navy RTSO) are separate systems whose interoperability relies on a common data layer that is still being built; joint and coalition exchange is largely manual.
unsolved_pain.evidence: Company and Army descriptions of interoperability goals for EWPMT-X, SSF and RTSO; DISA EMBM RFI seeking a joint common platform.
unsolved_pain.label: INFERENCE

unsolved_pain.pain: DoD-NTIA spectrum sharing studies lack transparency to stakeholders, implying weak shared tooling and data for coexistence and interference analysis.
unsolved_pain.evidence: GAO-26-107873 findings on collaboration and transparency gaps.
unsolved_pain.label: FACT

why_not_solved.explanation: Cheap wideband SDRs, edge GPUs and RF ML matured after 2018; the Army's 2014-era EWPMT architecture predates them, and the sensor density needed for an EM COP only became affordable around 2023-2025 (Distributed Spectrum, MOTH).

Sensors (PEO IEW&S programs and REWSI), planning software (EWPMT-X), enterprise spectrum data (DISA DSO GEMSIS), joint EMBM (DISA/JEMSOC), and C-UAS passive sensing (JIATF-401) are bought by different offices with different vehicles; no single buyer owns the end-to-end spectrum picture.

EWPMT was a single-prime development; GEMSIS/Spectrum XXI is a decades-old code base; sensor vendors expose proprietary formats. The move to TAK (EWPMT-X) is the Army's explicit fix, which also lowers the barrier for third-party plugins.

Adversary emitter parametrics, EW mission data and much SIGINT-derived detection live in classified enclaves, so a commercial startup cannot build or test the highest-value fusion without cleared staff and facilities.

Fusing detections from heterogeneous sensors with different time bases, security labels and formats into TAK, EWPMT and JSDR while under DDIL is an integration problem no single vendor has been contracted to own.

Outside DoD, spectrum monitoring buyers (regulators, telcos, ranges) are few and price-sensitive; Aurora Insight's RF-mapping-as-data model ended in a Maxar acquisition rather than scale, so venture capital historically avoided the segment until 2024-2025.
Army, USMC, Navy, Air Force and DISA each have their own spectrum tools and data layers; a joint solution requires governance that GAO (2021) and AOC (2026) say is still missing.

attractiveness.bull: 2026 shows real money moving from prototypes to production for low-cost spectrum sensors (REWSI ~$196M IDIQs, Hidden Level $100M OTA) and the Army has publicly re-platformed its EW planning stack onto the open TAK framework, creating a plugin ecosystem a small team can enter. Own-signature awareness (S2AS) is unclassified, urgent (Ukraine lessons) and heading to a rapid fielding decision; interference geolocation is dual-use with regulators and spectrum-sharing needs (GAO-26-107873). Venture investors are now funding the space (Distributed Spectrum $25M Series A, March 2025).
attractiveness.bear: The obvious sensor-network play already has funded, contracted leaders (Distributed Spectrum, Heaviside, RII, Hidden Level, Anduril Pulsar) and the Army just wrote nine-figure ceilings to two of them; the software/COP layer is being absorbed into government-owned TAK and DISA's EMBM-J, shrinking the room for a proprietary product; most high-value fusion requires classified emitter data and cleared people; and anything labeled EW/DF for military use is likely USML Category XI, which is a serious problem for a founding team with a non-U.S.-person co-founder. Ceilings are not revenue: REWSI and OTA figures are ceilings with unknown obligations.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium attractiveness overall; low for a hardware sensor-network startup entering in late 2026, medium for a narrowly scoped unclassified software wedge (own-signature awareness or interference geolocation delivered as a TAK plugin and sensor-agnostic fusion service), contingent on resolving export-control structure before writing any EW-specific code.

signal_sequence.event: prototype award - Raytheon EWPMT development begins (RECALL)
follow-on / limited fielding - Raven Claw laptop variant of EWPMT
strategy and oversight - DoD EMS Superiority Strategy; GAO-21-64 on EMSO governance; TLS-BCT prototype OTA (RECALL)
prototype award - Lockheed TLS-EAB prototype; STRATCOM creates JEMSOC; DISA releases cloud EMS visualization tool (Dec 2023)
re-plan - EWPMT RS3 task order competition cancelled, EWPMT-X TAK pilot; TLS-BCT funding realigned to manpack; DISA GEMSIS sustainment sources sought (Sept); EMBM RFI

sources sought and prototype testing - S2AS FY25 new start sources sought; S2AS in TiC exercises; division EW prototypes; Distributed Spectrum Series A (Mar); Epirus Gen II $43.5M (Jul); Army FY26 EMFP $9.1M request

production - REWSI call for solutions (Apr) then $99M and $96.9M production IDIQs (Aug 27, Sep 3); Hidden Level $100M OTA (Aug 5); GAO-26-107873 (Jun); AOC JEMSO CSA proposal (Feb); S2AS rapid fielding decision targeted Q2 FY26

market_stage.rationale: Sensors have crossed from prototype to production-type vehicles in 2026 (repeat orders not yet observable), while the planning/COP software layer is mid-transition (EWPMT-X pilot, S2AS rapid fielding decision pending) and the enterprise spectrum-management layer is in sustainment-plus-enhancement mode. That mix is Transitioning, not Mature.

proto_purgatory.notes: EWPMT ran ~10 years of capability drops (2014-2024) and ended with a cancelled follow-on and a re-host on TAK; TLS-BCT was restructured repeatedly; MFEW-AL is entering service roughly seven years after its prototype award. Distributed Spectrum's public traction is a series of sub-$10M awards. Counter-signal: in 2026 the Army broke purgatory for sensors by issuing production IDIQs within five months of a call for solutions, and DoD issued a $100M OTA to Hidden Level.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Both. Sensors are exiting purgatory (opportunity for sensor-agnostic software riding the newly bought fleet), but planning/COP software is where purgatory has been chronic (warning: a proprietary EMBM product risks repeating EWPMT's fate unless delivered as a TAK plugin the government can own and re-compete).

candidate_gaps.title: Sensor-agnostic own-signature and EM COP fusion layer delivered as a TAK plugin
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Units are about to receive thousands of heterogeneous cheap spectrum sensors (MOTH, Dragonfly, manpacks, S2AS kits) but there is no government-owned, sensor-agnostic software layer that fuses them into a real-time own-signature and threat-emitter picture inside TAK/EWPMT-X under DDIL.
candidate_gaps.user: Brigade and division CEMA sections, EW platoon leaders, command post signals/spectrum managers
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) EW platoon runs manpack or fixed sensors and reads vendor GUIs; 2) detections are typed or screenshotted into chat/ATAK as CoT points; 3) spectrum manager compares against a spreadsheet or Spectrum XXI export of friendly assignments; 4) CEMA officer builds a PowerPoint/EWPMT overlay of the EM picture for the commander; 5) own-signature checks require an external red team or a dedicated S2AS demo kit; 6) higher echelons receive the picture by voice or email hours later.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: EWPMT/Raven Claw (being replaced), S2AS prototypes (rapid fielding decision pending), vendor-specific apps (Lattice for Pulsar, CACI kit software), ATAK with ad hoc plugins.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Vendor lock-in per sensor, no common detection schema, no time-synchronized fusion, stale picture under DDIL, and the government now owns the framework (TAK) but not the fusion logic.

evidence.claim: Army cancelled EWPMT follow-on and is re-hosting EW planning and spectrum management on TAK (EWPMT-X) with USMC for FY2026.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: S2AS is an FY25 new start seeking COTS/NDI hardware and software for own-signature sensing and visualization, with a rapid fielding decision targeted Q2 FY26.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Army awarded ~$196M in production IDIQs for two different sensor types from two different vendors within one week (Aug 27 and Sep 3, 2026), multiplying heterogeneous sensor feeds.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Raven Claw was created because EWPMT needed a host server and reliable connectivity, i.e., DDIL operation was an unmet requirement.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Brigades previously could not see their own EW footprint until a new tool arrived in late 2024.
evidence.label: INFERENCE

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Sensor startups monetize hardware and keep fusion proprietary (Lattice, Distributed Spectrum cloud); software-only entrants lacked exercise access and a government-owned host until TAK became the Army's declared EW framework in 2024.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High: the EWPMT-X integrator (unknown) or Anduril could deliver the same plugin; TAK Product Center may build a reference fusion service; sensor vendors can ship their own TAK plugins.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: An open detection schema plus DDIL-tolerant CRDT-style sync and lightweight TDOA/AoA fusion that runs on a squad laptop or Android and degrades gracefully, with own-signature scoring as the first killer feature.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: ATAK/WinTAK plugin plus TAK Server microservice ingesting SigMF/CoT detections from KrakenSDR and USRP nodes, rendering friendly-emitter heatmaps and a command-post signature score; demo at a National Guard or ROTC field exercise, then apply to an AFWERX/Army xTech or SBIR open topic.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Unclassified for own-signature (friendly emissions recorded under CUI at exercises); CUI/classified for threat emitter ID later.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: TAK plugin certification, CoT schema, later EWPMT-X APIs and JSDR/Spectrum XXI export import; sensor vendor APIs.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: SBIR/STTR (requires majority U.S. ownership), AFWERX open topic, Army xTech, TAK Product Center collaboration, subcontract to a REWSI awardee.
candidate_gaps.why_now: TAK re-platforming (2024-2026), S2AS rapid fielding decision (FY26), REWSI production sensors arriving (2026-2029), Ukraine signature-targeting lessons.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Government treats fusion as part of EWPMT-X scope and awards it to the incumbent integrator, or Anduril bundles it free with Pulsar; plus ITAR Category XI exposure once the plugin ingests threat detections.

candidate_gaps.title: Tactical-edge spectrum management and EMI resolution workflow (JRFL, assignments, interference tickets) that works disconnected from Spectrum XXI
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Brigade and division spectrum managers still build frequency plans, JRFLs and interference reports with enterprise tools that need reach-back to DISA's legacy Spectrum XXI/JSDR, so they fall back to spreadsheets and email in DDIL conditions.
candidate_gaps.user: Army 25E spectrum managers, USMC spectrum managers, JFMO staff, Navy afloat spectrum managers
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Receive unit task organization and radio/sensor inventories; 2) request assignments via Spectrum XXI (online or offline sync) to NTIA/host nation; 3) build the JRFL in spreadsheets and EWPMT; 4) receive EMI reports by voice/chat; 5) manually triage against assignments and EW schedules; 6) re-enter results into JSDR when connectivity returns.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Spectrum XXI / SXXI-Online, JSDR, E2ESS, EWPMT spectrum module, USMC Spectrum Services Framework, Navy RTSO/AESOP, DISA cloud EMBM tool (Dec 2023).
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Legacy code base in sustainment, enterprise hosting, poor tactical usability, no integration with sensed reality (what is actually on the air), and manual re-entry between service tools.

evidence.claim: DISA sought sources for GEMSIS (Spectrum XXI, JSDR, E2ESS, ISD) sustainment and enhancement in Sept 2024, confirming the enterprise stack is legacy in sustainment.

evidence.claim: DISA DSO issued an RFI for a joint Electromagnetic Battle Management system, indicating current tools do not provide a common EMSO SA and C2 platform.

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: The data of record (JSDR) is government-held CUI inside DISA; the buyer is a single agency program with an entrenched sustainment contractor; the user base is small (a few thousand spectrum managers), so venture returns look thin.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: Medium-high: DISA EMBM-J is the sanctioned answer; a startup would be a subcontractor or TAK plugin at best.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Offline-first JRFL/assignment/EMI-ticket app that syncs with Spectrum XXI exports (SFAF) and shows sensed occupancy from G1-style sensors, closing the plan-versus-reality loop.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Web/Android app with SFAF import, propagation-aware conflict checks and EMI ticketing, piloted with a National Guard signal battalion; requires government furnished sample data.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: SFAF/JSDR records (CUI), unit radio inventories; can start with synthetic and exercise data.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Spectrum XXI import/export, TAK, EWPMT-X, EMBM-J APIs (undefined publicly).
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: DISA or Army SBIR, subcontract to GEMSIS sustainment awardee, USMC SSF pilot.
candidate_gaps.why_now: EMBM-J build-out and GEMSIS enhancement re-compete window 2025-2027; EWPMT-X pilot invites TAK components.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Small, captive buyer; classification of assignment data; DISA may not accept third-party clients against JSDR.

candidate_gaps.title: Interference and rogue-emitter geolocation from networked low-cost SDRs for installations, ranges and shared bands (dual-use)
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Bases, test ranges, border sectors and shared-spectrum bands need persistent, affordable detection and geolocation of interference and unknown emitters, and current solutions are either expensive premium monitoring networks or bespoke passive-sensing vendors.
candidate_gaps.user: Installation spectrum managers, range control, C-UAS cells (JIATF-401), DoD CIO spectrum sharing analysts, FCC/NTIA enforcement, telecom operators
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Interference complaint arrives; 2) technician drives with a handheld analyzer or deploys a rented CRFS/R&S node; 3) manual DF and triangulation over days; 4) report filed to spectrum manager; 5) for drones, separate C-UAS sensors (Hidden Level, Dedrone) with their own dashboards.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: CRFS RFeye networks, R&S/Keysight monitoring, Hidden Level (now scaling under $100M OTA), Distributed Spectrum, Dedrone/Axon, KrakenSDR by hobbyists and some units.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Cost per node, calibration and time sync at scale, false alarms in dense urban RF, and separate stacks for interference vs drones vs EW.

evidence.claim: DoD awarded Hidden Level a $100M OTA to scale passive RF sensing around installations, ranges and border sections, proving demand for persistent passive sensing at scale.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: GAO-26-107873 found DoD and NTIA spectrum sharing studies lacked transparency, and such sharing requires monitoring and interference resolution in shared bands.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Distributed Spectrum raised $25M Series A (Mar 2025) on a distributed low-cost sensor thesis after >$7M contracts in late 2024 - investor and early government interest, not proof of production.

evidence.claim: Aurora Insight's RF-mapping business exited to Maxar in Jan 2023 without evident military scale, a warning that data-only models underperform.
evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Several are trying (Hidden Level, Distributed Spectrum, CRFS) and the leaders are now capitalized; the remaining gap is at the low-cost, software-defined, multi-mission end and in the dual-use regulator/telecom market, which is price-sensitive.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High: Hidden Level and Distributed Spectrum can move down-market; CRFS can cut price.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Self-calibrating TDOA/AoA over commodity SDRs with ML false-alarm suppression, sold as software plus reference hardware for installation spectrum managers, with a commercial path via FCC/NTIA and 5G operators.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: 6-node KrakenSDR/USRP network on a university campus geolocating ISM-band and LTE interference sources; publish accuracy results; pilot with an Army National Guard installation or a test range.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Unclassified RF captures; installation emitter lists (CUI when DoD).
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Export to TAK/CoT and to installation C-UAS C2 (FAAD C2 / Forward Area Air Defense) via open interfaces.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: AFWERX open topic, NSIN, DHS/CBP or FCC pilots, telecom customers.
candidate_gaps.why_now: Shared-band sharing studies, drone incursions at bases, Hidden Level OTA validating the category.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Competing head-on with two funded, contracted leaders on a hardware-adjacent product with $250k of capital.
